rationale: Neither candidate surfaces the actual human review thread's core concerns (whether functional tests are now redundant given perf coverage, and the intentional narrowing of source_file_dependencies to MiniCPM-owned files only) — both instead recommend re-adding run_benchmark.py/conftest.py to the dependency list, which the real author explicitly rejected as noise from shared infra, so recall is low and that specific finding is contextually wrong for both. Both are well-grounded with real line citations and verified claims (assert-baseline dead code, missing artifact upload, mismatched baseline sweep points), giving decent precision, but X presents a clean, prioritized Major/Should-fix/Minor review with experimentally verified claims, while Y buries its findings under a redundant, semi-duplicated validation dump that hurts readability and actionability.
